newsitem.title: FRANCE: Striking French truckers lift Calais blockade.
newsitem.headline: Striking French truckers lift Calais blockade.

text.p: Striking French truck drivers lifted a roadblock at the main Channel port of Calais on Friday, allowing stranded British and foreign trucks to board ferries for England, the Chamber of Commerce said.

Strikers from the Communist-led CGT and the Force Ouvriere unions decided to resume work, judging they had won enough from employers in a 12-day strike over pensions, pay and working hours, the officials said.
The strikers had been blocking the port to trucks since Sunday but had allowed cars and passengers to board as normal.
On Thursday, the strikers relaxed their grip to let 200 waiting trucks to board ferries bound for Dover but reimposed the blockade later in the day.
The British embassy said several hundred British drivers were still stranded in France on Friday, as were thousands of other foreign trucks.

The 12-day strike was on the verge of concluding around France after unions signed an early retirement deal with bosses and consulted their members at roadblocks on ending the action that has brought fuel rationing and other shortages.
